name: Fapfap
description: Fapfap, known as Agram in Niger and Mali, is a simple yet strategic last-trick-only game from West Africa. Players compete to win the final trick after five rounds of play, with the unusual twist that winning earlier tricks can be a disadvantage as it forces you to lead and cede control. A stripped 35-card deck is used, with unique ranking and the removal of the Ace of Spades.

content.text: Fapfap, known as Agram in Niger and Mali, is a simple yet strategic last-trick-only game from West Africa. Players compete to win the final trick after five rounds of play, with the unusual twist that winning earlier tricks can be a disadvantage as it forces you to lead and cede control. A stripped 35-card deck is used, with unique ranking and the removal of the Ace of Spades.

Originating in the Sahel region of West Africa, Fapfap evolved from European trick-taking games introduced during the colonial era. The game is known by different names across the region: Agram in Niger and Mali, Sink-Sink in parts of Niger, and Fapfap in Cameroon. It is closely related to Sparrow in Ghana.
35-card stripped deck. Take a standard 52-card deck and remove: all Kings, all Queens, all Jacks, all 2s, and the Ace of Spades (The Chief). Remaining deck: Ace (except Spades), 3-10 of all suits.
Deck and chips/stakes for optional scoring variant.

Dealer (rotates clockwise) shuffles; right-hand player cuts. Dealer distributes 5 or 6 cards to each player (depending on regional variant) in two batches. Cameroon: 6 cards (3, then 3). Niger: 5 cards (3, then 2).

items.text: Agram (Niger): Standard version with 6 cards dealt (3, then 3). Winner of 6th trick wins.
Sink-Sink (Niger): Identical to Agram except only 5 cards dealt (3, then 2). Winner of 5th trick wins.
Fapfap (Cameroon): 5 or 6 cards dealt. Includes scoring multipliers: winning final trick with a 3 = double stake; two consecutive tricks with 3's = quadruple stake.
Agram (Mali): 31-card deck (removes 6-2 of all suits, plus Ace of Spades). Unusual rank order: A-K-10-Q-9-8-J-7. 5 cards dealt (2, then 3).
Sparrow (Ghana): Related game with different deck composition and regional rule modifications.
